newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Troops intensify search after fresh Timor battle.
newsitem.headline: Troops intensify search after fresh Timor battle.

text.p: Indonesian troops intensified their hunt for separatists in East Timor on Monday after a fresh gunbattle on Sunday with guerrillas who killed 17 security force members in a weekend ambush, police sources said.

"There was a fresh gunbattle in Baucau yesterday afternoon which involved troops and the rebels. But none of rebels was arrested and there were also no casualties among the troops," the source, who asked not to be named, told Reuters from the East Timor capital, Dili.
"The search has been intensified. In general, Dili and the other surrounding areas are quiet," the source added. He declined to give other details.
Military officials could not be reached for comment.
Police said at least 34 people had died since last Wednesday as a result of separatist efforts to disrupt general elections in East Timor and the aftermath in the worst upsurge in violence in years.

Guerrillas are fighting Jakarta's rule in the former Portuguese colony occupied by Indonesia in 1975 and annexed as its 27th province the following year. The United Nations still does not recognise the move. Police said separatists killed 16 policemen and a soldier on Saturday morning in a grenade and gun attack on a unit that had been providing security for last Thursday's general elections.
The military blamed the deaths on an operational mistake that left the unit vulnerable to attack. Normally two trucks are used to cover each other, but in this case there was only one vehicle.

The ruling Golkar won a sweeping victory in the elections, taking over 74 percent of the national vote. It won 84 percent of the ballots cast in East Timor, where 81 percent of the electorate voted despite the violence. Police said another 17 people, including at least four rebels, died last Wednesday and Thursday in election related violence.

The Indonesian military, which maintains a strong presence in East Timor, says about 80 poorly armed guerrillas remain in the rugged hills in the territory. Other sources suggest there are around 200.
Jakarta officially has five full battalions of troops as well as other units in East Timor numbering around 5,000 men, far more than in neighbouring provinces with much larger populations.
